//: Each command tries three interpreter names in turn.
This is safe ONLY because every script here exits 0 unconditionally —
including guard_secrets.py's deny path, which signals refusal in its JSON
output rather than its exit code. So the `||` chain can fire only when the
interpreter itself is missing, never because a script did its job.
Why bother: `python` is not always on PATH on Windows (the py launcher may
be the only entry point), and on some Linux distributions only `python3`
exists. A hook that silently never runs is worse than no hook, because it
is still trusted — and the PreToolUse guard here is a security control.
